entries.name: Strichartz estimates without loss outside two strictly convex obstacles
entries.abstract: We prove global Strichartz estimates without loss outside two strictly convex obstacles, combining arguments from M.Ikawa (1982,1988) with more recent ones inspired by N.Burq, C.Guillarmou, and A. Hassell (2010) and O. Ivanovici (2010). This is to be contrasted with the loss in the smoothing estimate for the Schrödinger equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions in the presence of a trapped geodesic.

entries.name: A Chebotarev Density Theorem over Local Fields
entries.abstract: We compute the $p$-adic densities of points with a given splitting type along a (generically) finite map, analogous to the classical Chebotarev theorem over number fields and function fields. Under some mild hypotheses, we prove that these densities satisfy a functional equation in the size of the residue field. This functional equation is a direct reflection of Poincaré duality in étale cohomology. As a consequence, we prove a conjecture of Bhargava, Cremona, Fisher, and Gajović on factorization densities of p-adic polynomials. The key tool is the notion of admissible pairs associated to a group, which we use as an invariant of the inertia and decomposition action of a local field on the fibers of the finite map. We compute the splitting densities by Möbius inverting certain p-adic integrals along the poset of admissible pairs. The conjecture on factorization densities follows immediately for tamely ramified primes from our general results. We reduce the complete conjecture to the existence of an explicit "Tate-type" resolution of the "resultant locus" over the integers and complete the proof of the conjecture by constructing this resolution.

entries.name: Selective Inference for Survey-Weighted Generalized Linear Models: Growing Dimension and Average Marginal Effects
entries.abstract: This paper extends the $\ell_1$-penalized likelihood Selective Inference method to survey settings. We establish its asymptotic validity for generalized linear models with an increasing number of covariates and survey weights, allowing inference on pseudo-true parameters of possibly misspecified selected models. Moreover, we generalize the method to facilitate inference on nonlinear functionals, such as the average marginal effect in survey-weighted logit models. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is illustrated using simulated data and the 2020 Canadian Internet Use Survey.

entries.name: Harary's Sum and Integral Sum Graphs -- A Survey in detail
entries.abstract: Harary introduced the concepts of sum and integral sum graphs. A graph $G$ is a {\em sum graph} if the vertices of $G$ can be labeled with distinct positive integers so that $e = uv$ is an edge of $G$ if and only if the sum of the labels on vertices $u$ and $v$ is also a label in $G$. An {\em integral sum graph} is also defined just as sum graph, the difference being that the labels may be any distinct integers. This survey presents results obtained by different authors, in detail, on sum and integral sum graphs.

entries.name: On proving an Inequality of Ramanujan using Explicit Order Estimates for the Mertens Function
entries.abstract: We intend to prove unconditionally that the Ramanujan's Inequality, \begin{align*} π(x)^2<\frac{ex}{\log x}π(x/e) \end{align*} for every real $x\geq e^{490}$, where $π(x)$ counts the primes up to $x$. We try to obtain an order estimate for $ψ(x)-x$ explicitly based on a point-wise power bound on the Mertens function $M(x)$, where $ψ$ is the second Chebyshev function. An asymmetric hyperbola decomposition of the logarithmically weighted Mertens sum and partial summation give an exact cancellation at the split point. Using the zero-free half-plane, $\Re (s)>7/8$ for the Riemann zeta function, we prove $|M(t)|\leq12000\,t^{213/235}$ for $t\geq e^{131}$ by averaged Perron inversion. The resulting bounds for $ψ$ and the prime counting function $π$ gives us our desired result. A separate argument using a classical zero-free region proves the asymptotic inequality.

entries.name: Asymptotics of a Gauss hypergeometric function related to moments of symmetric square L-functions I
entries.abstract: We prove an asymptotic formula for a special case of the Gauss hypergeometric function, which arises in the explicit formula for the second moment of Maass form symmetric-square $L$-functions.

entries.name: Rectifying Conformity Scores for Better Conditional Coverage
entries.abstract: We present a new method for generating confidence sets within the split conformal prediction framework. Our method performs a trainable transformation of any given conformity score to improve conditional coverage while ensuring exact marginal coverage. The transformation is based on an estimate of the conditional quantile of conformity scores. The resulting method is particularly beneficial for constructing adaptive confidence sets in multi-output problems where standard conformal quantile regression approaches have limited applicability. We develop a theoretical bound that captures the influence of the accuracy of the quantile estimate on the approximate conditional validity, unlike classical bounds for conformal prediction methods that only offer marginal coverage. We experimentally show that our method is highly adaptive to the local data structure and outperforms existing methods in terms of conditional coverage, improving the reliability of statistical inference in various applications.

entries.name: Campana separable rational connectedness of toric orbifold
entries.abstract: Campana introduced a notion of Campana rational connectedness for Campana orbifolds and conjectured that certain Fano orbifolds are Campana rationally connected. In this paper, we study a version of this conjecture in positive characteristic and verify a stronger statement for some toric orbifolds. We also provide examples illustrating the relation between the failure of separable Campana rational connectedness and singularities.

entries.name: On the future cover of a sofic shift
entries.abstract: The paper contains a new proof of the theorem by Krieger which establishes the canonicity of the future cover of a sofic shift. In addition the paper describes a method to produce new canonical covers from a given one, resulting in canonical covers related to, but generally different from the future cover.

entries.name: Correcting quantum errors one gradient step at a time
entries.abstract: Probabilistic approximate quantum error correction (PAQEC) lets a recovery fail with some probability, in exchange for higher fidelity when it succeeds. Prior PAQEC code searches keep the codewords orthonormal with penalty terms and tune the code without its best recovery. We propose a gradient method with three new parts. First, the codewords move on the complex Stiefel manifold, so they are orthonormal at every step without penalties. Second, every code is trained against its best recovery, which we solve for at each step rather than learn. Third, a fast Petz recovery that we can differentiate even for symmetric codes gets the search close, and the exact semidefinite program finishes it. We train a single five-qubit code over generalized amplitude damping noise. At weak noise ($γ= 0.1$, $p = 0.05$) and equal success probability, it has $23$ times lower infidelity than the permutation-invariant code of prior work, and $9$ times lower than that work's numerically optimized code. At equal fidelity it succeeds $91\%$ of the time, against $76\%$ for the permutation-invariant code.

entries.name: Elementary Quantum Gates from Lie Group Embeddings in $U(2^n)$: Spectral Geometry and Intrinsic Factorization Lengths
entries.abstract: We study intrinsic factorizations of quantum gates using determinant-one unitaries supported on arbitrary two-dimensional subspaces of $\C^N$, where $N=2^n$. For $U\in U(N)$ write $r=\operatorname{rank}(U-I)$. When $r\ge2$, we characterize all factors that lower the active rank by two through traceless compressions of the Cayley transform on $\Ran(U-I)$. For the ordered active eigenangles $\vartheta_j\in(0,2π)$, existence is equivalent to $\vartheta_1+\vartheta_2\le2π\le\vartheta_{r-1}+\vartheta_r$. For $U\in SU(N)$, combining this construction with eigenangle merging realizes the classical reflection-length formula in two-level form: $\ell^{SU}(U)=\max\{ν(U),r-ν(U)\}$, where $ν(U)$ is the positive eigenangle sum divided by $2π$. On the full-rank open set, the age indexes $N-1$ connected components with constant intrinsic length. We place these factorizations within the spectral description of the dictionaries formed by faithful $SU(2)$ and $U(2)$ embeddings. For $n\ge2$, these dictionaries are Haar-null of Hausdorff dimensions $N^2-N+1$ and $N^2-N+2$; the former is compact and the latter dense. Distances to compact sectors reduce to eigenvalue matching. Further results concern ambient minimality of embedded geodesics and a first-order sharp spectral bound on coherence production.

entries.name: Log canonical thresholds at infinity
entries.abstract: The paper considers a global version of the notion of log canonical threshold for plurisubharmonic functions $u$ of logarithmic growth in $\mathbb{C}^n$, aiming at description of the range of all $p>0$ such that $e^{-u}\in L^p(\mathbb{C}^n)$. Explicit formulas are obtained in the toric case. By considering Bergman functions of corresponding weighted Hilbert spaces, a new polynomial approximation of plurisubharmonic functions of logarithmic growth with control over its singularities and behavior at infinity (a global version of Demailly's approximation theorem) is established. Some application to tame polynomial maps are given.

entries.name: Real-Time Dynamic N-1 Screening: Identifying High-Risk Lines and Transformers After Common Faults
entries.abstract: Power system operators routinely perform N-1 contingency analysis, yet conventional tools provide limited guidance on which lines or transformers deserve heightened attention during fast post-fault transients. In particular, static screening does not reveal whether (1) the same faulted line repeatedly triggers severe downstream overloads, or (2) a specific transformer emerges as vulnerable across many distinct fault scenarios. This paper introduces a real-time dynamic N-1 screening framework that addresses this gap by estimating, for each counterfactual single-phase transmission fault, the probability of transient overcurrent on critical grid elements. The output is an operator-facing dashboard that ranks (a) faulted lines whose outages most frequently lead to dangerous transformer overloads, and (b) transformers that consistently overload across top-risk scenarios, both of which are actionable indicators for real-time situational awareness. The approach models post-fault electromechanical dynamics using a linear stochastic formulation of the swing equations with short-lived, fault-localized uncertainty, and combines analytic transient evaluation with cross-entropy based importance sampling to efficiently estimate rare but high-impact events. All N-1 contingencies are evaluated in parallel with linear computational complexity. The framework is demonstrated on the IEEE 118-bus system, where it reveals latent high-risk lines and transformers that remain invisible under deterministic dynamic or static N-1 analysis. Results show orders-of-magnitude computational speedup relative to brute-force Monte Carlo, enabling practical deployment within real-time operational cycles.

entries.name: The Ferrers bound for spanning trees in bipartite graphs
entries.abstract: We prove Ehrenborg's conjecture that every connected bipartite graph $G$ with parts of size $m$ and $n$ has at most $\frac{1}{mn}\prod_{v\in V(G)} \operatorname{deg}(v)$ spanning trees, and that equality holds if and only if $G$ is a Ferrers graph.

entries.name: A Non-graded Koszul Duality and Its Applications
entries.abstract: Let \(Λ\) be a finite-dimensional Koszul algebra with Koszul dual \(Λ^!\). We establish derived Koszul dualities at the level of bounded derived categories, both in the graded setting \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(Λ\textup{-gmod})\) and in the ungraded setting \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(Λ\textup{-mod})\). We first prove a graded derived Koszul duality for every finite-dimensional Koszul algebra, with no Noetherian or coherence assumptions on the Koszul dual. We then show that the bounded derived category \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(Λ\textup{-mod})\) can be reconstructed from the graded theory as the triangulated hull of an orbit category. This yields a genuinely non-graded derived Koszul duality. We further establish singular and dg refinements of these dualities. For Iwanaga--Gorenstein Koszul algebras, this gives a stable Koszul duality for graded Gorenstein-projective modules and their ungraded counterparts, providing a non-graded form of the Bernstein--Gel'fand--Gel'fand correspondence. As applications, we obtain new descriptions of the bounded derived categories \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(\mathcal{O}_λ)\) for all integral blocks of category \(\mathcal{O}\), including singular blocks, which are non-graded counterparts of the Koszul dualities of Beilinson, Ginzburg, and Soergel. We also establish analogous dualities for certain categories of perverse sheaves arising in geometric representation theory. Finally, we formulate conjectural descriptions of bounded derived and singularity categories of finite-dimensional graded algebras in terms of dg orbit categories.

entries.name: Structure-Aware Tensorial Model Reduction
entries.abstract: This work investigates a two-stage method for constructing projection-based reduced-order models (ROMs) of parameterized partial differential equations (PDEs). Based on established tensorial ROM methodology, the proposed approach reduces dimensionality offline by encoding solution snapshots using a multi-linear Tucker factorization, so that a reduced basis which varies nonlinearly with PDE parameters can be rapidly constructed online and used in a Galerkin ROM. Two novel extensions of this strategy, tailored to the cases of structured PDEs and sparse parameter sampling, are presented: the construction of reduced bases orthonormalized with respect to a general discrete inner product, and the interpolation of encoded states via radial basis functions. Basic representation and ROM error estimates are presented demonstrating the validity of these modifications, and the approach is challenged on state-linear examples where monolithic-basis ROMs are known to struggle, including a realistic instance of Maxwell's equations in 3D. Results suggest that the proposed nonlinear basis ROM can effectively mitigate linear restrictions on Kolmogorov $n$-width while improving upon previous tensorial ROM technology, particularly in the highly nonlinear and data-limited regimes characteristic of practical use cases.

entries.name: On small-step quarter plane lattice walks with a non D-finite univariate generating function
entries.abstract: We report on the status of the conjecture of Bousquet-Mélou and Mishna that the univariate counting generating function of a small-step quarter-plane lattice model is D-finite if and only if a particular group associated to the walk is finite. While the finite-group case is fully resolved, the infinite-group case remains incomplete. First we survey the known cases. By invoking asymptotics results from probability theory and a case analysis completed by Bostan, Raschel and Salvy (2014), we establish that the generating functions of 14 infinite-group models are not D-finite, and that for an additional 18 models the generating function for walks that end on an axis is not D-finite. We conclude with a discussion of limitations of asymptotic arguments to resolve the remaining cases.

entries.name: Kalman structure and observability for transport systems
entries.abstract: We study observability and controllability for constant-coefficient first-order hyperbolic systems on the real line when only part of the state is observed or controlled. Even when the Kalman rank condition holds, the usual \(L^2(\mathbb R)^N\)-observability estimate may fail because some components are detected only through the dynamics. We show that the Kalman structure determines the appropriate observability estimate. A component that becomes visible after \(k\) algebraic steps is measured at low Fourier frequencies with a weight of order \(|ξ|^{2k}\) in the Fourier variable. This yields a natural Kalman-adapted observation space for the system. Assuming that the transport matrix \(A\) is diagonalizable over \(\mathbb R\), we prove whole-line observability in this space for every positive time and derive exact controllability in the corresponding dual space. If, in addition, \(A\) has no zero eigenvalue and the observation set satisfies the one-dimensional bounded-gap condition, we establish localized observability whenever the observation time exceeds the natural characteristic travel-time threshold. Separately, in the whole-line setting, we extend the construction to transport matrices \(A\) with real spectrum and possible nontrivial Jordan blocks.

entries.name: A Direction Adaptation Evolution Strategy for Noisy Derivative-Free Optimization
entries.abstract: In noisy derivative-free optimization (DFO), methods based on the matrix adaptation evolution strategy (MAES) often mistakenly identify points with spuriously good function values, undermining selection and leading to unreliable search directions. To address this, we develop a novel direction adaptation evolution strategy (DAES) that targets the algorithmic phases prone to noise propagation, combining selected-population search with complexity analysis. Fixing the transformation matrix to the identity, DAES employs a structured direction-generation mechanism consisting of symmetric sampling, joint sorting--selection of noisy values, partitioning of all sampled directions into three ranked groups, and construction of a heuristic search direction. Along this direction, a noisy derivative-free sufficient descent condition with extrapolation is applied. Using a probabilistic angle condition preserved through our proposed framework, we obtain, to the best of our knowledge, the first high-probability evaluation-complexity bounds for a noisy MAES-type method across nonconvex, convex, and strongly convex objectives, under bounded noise. Finally, experiments on 230 BARON BCP problems across eight noise levels compare DAES with five DFO solvers, notably MADFO, showing greater robustness at intermediate-to-small budgets.

entries.name: One Shot, Twenty-One Balls: A Computer-Assisted Proof of a Single-Stroke Total Clearance in an Idealized Model of Snooker
entries.abstract: Snooker folklore holds that no single stroke can pocket all twenty-one object balls. We examine the claim in an explicit model: twenty-two equal disks on a rectangle with six pocket points, under constant rolling deceleration, frictionless collisions with normal restitution, and lossy specular cushions. We exhibit a configuration and a stroke, and prove in interval arithmetic that every stroke in an explicit box around it pockets all twenty-one object balls, so the set of successful strokes has positive measure. That set is a ribbon: every speed from 9.3214 to 12 m/s works, while the certified window of directions is 9.481e-43 radians wide, a number explained by a first-order analysis of twenty near-grazing collisions. A second configuration, a near-frozen cluster, has a certified window 9.4e-4 radians wide, thirty-nine orders of magnitude wider; its certificate uses Taylor models of degree six. The strokes with a given list of events form a semialgebraic set, and the endpoints of the windows are algebraic points of the circle. For the regulation opening position we state the corresponding conjecture, and show that if it holds with a regular witness then a finite certified search establishes it.

entries.name: Approximate Message Passing with Random Initialization for Phase Retrieval
entries.abstract: Randomly initialized first-order iterative algorithms are simple, widely used, and empirically effective across many high-dimensional inference problems, yet their theoretical behavior remains far less understood than that of algorithms started from more elaborate, problem-specific initializations such as spectral initialization. This paper takes a step toward closing this gap by studying randomly initialized approximate message passing (AMP) for noiseless phase retrieval, a canonical nonconvex inference problem. We give a non-asymptotic, growing-horizon characterization of the AMP trajectory from random initialization, and show that it achieves both the information-theoretic weak recovery threshold $δ_{\rm weak}=1/2$ and the AMP strong recovery threshold $δ_{\rm str}\approx1.13$, matching the recovery thresholds established for spectrally initialized AMP. The key technical ingredients are twofold: (i) a non-asymptotic coupling that decomposes the AMP iterates as a signal component, a linear combination of independent Gaussian vectors, and an approximation error, and (ii) a second-order analysis of the Onsager correction error built around a non-asymptotic version of Bolthausen's condition. These allow us to analyze the $O_δ(\log n)$ steps required for weak recovery, and to faithfully track the asymptotic state evolution up to $n^{1/3}/\operatorname{polylog}(n)$ steps in the intermediate recovery regime $δ\in(δ_{\rm weak},δ_{\rm str})$, both beyond the $O(1)$-iteration horizon of classical AMP theory. Above the strong recovery threshold, AMP reaches any prescribed fixed recovery accuracy within $O_{δ,\varepsilon}(\log n)$ iterations. Both the coupling and the error analysis are developed for a broad class of generalized AMP dynamics and may be of independent interest for general single-index models.

entries.name: The Shadow Price of Intelligence: Quality Degradation and Retry Feedback in LLM Inference
entries.abstract: Large language model providers are compute constrained, and a common response to congestion is to degrade service: route queries to smaller models, cut reasoning budgets, or shorten context windows. A user who receives an unsatisfactory answer either retries, adding load while the system is busy, or abandons, possibly as churn. We model inference serving as a control problem in which service quality is the provider's decision. A two-regime fluid approximation with retries folded into the service rate gives closed-form trajectories and crossing times, so the dynamic program over quality tiers needs no simulation. We characterize a region in which a weaker tier uses less energy per task but more capacity per task, and show that in the fluid model reactive throttling to such a tier can keep the queue from draining. With heterogeneous customers the problem is a transportation problem with retry-inflated capacity coefficients; optimal routing follows a $cμ$-type index, and the dual of the capacity constraint gives the marginal cost of one more query by class and time. We illustrate the method on five instances calibrated to public benchmark data.

entries.name: Principal component error in high-dimensional factor models
entries.abstract: In a statistical factor model, principal components (or eigenvectors) of a sample covariance matrix serve as estimates of principal directions, the true drivers of co-movement of a collection of observed variables. We write the often substantial error in these estimates as a sum of two interpretable terms, which we show have almost sure asymptotic limits as the number of variables grows with sample size bounded. This scenario is commonplace in financial economics, genomics, machine learning and signal processing. Out-of-subspace error measures the distance from an estimate to the subspace spanned by population factor exposures. It can be expressed in terms of data, providing an estimable floor for asymptotic error. In-subspace error is driven by a rotation error within that subspace, which arises from the fixed sample size of the latent factor returns and cannot be estimated from data alone. We illustrate our error analysis with a three-factor simulation of the US public equity market, showing the dependence of the magnitude of the error and its components on dimension and sample size. In that simulation, out-of-subspace error dominates. Researchers who rely on principal component analysis to estimate factor models can use our results to quantify errors in model-based predictions and attributions.

entries.name: Strictly positive optimal Hardy weights on manifolds and graphs via Green potential
entries.abstract: Consider a subcritical functional $Q$ associated with a $p$-Schrödinger operator defined on a domain $Ω$ in a noncompact Riemannian manifold. Employing the supersolution construction, we obtain a family of strictly positive-critical Hardy weights for $Q$. The construction is based on the Green potential $G_f$, with a strictly positive charge $f$ such that $G_f$ vanishes at infinity. An interesting new feature of this family, depending on a parameter $0\leq \varepsilon\leq 1$, is the transition from positive-criticality to null-criticality at $\varepsilon=0$. Furthermore, we prove an analogous result on graphs.

entries.name: On separable pairs of fields and beautiful pairs of separably closed valued fields
entries.abstract: We continue the study of beautiful pairs of henselian valued fields, initiated in joint work of the second author with Cubides Kovacsics and Ye. As our main result, we show that separably closed non-trivially valued fields of arbitrary imperfection degree admit beautiful pairs associated to natural subclasses of all bounded definable types, most notably for all definable types orthogonal to the value group and for all bounded definable types. These beautiful pairs are elementary pairs satisfying certain natural axioms. They satisfy beauty transfer, i.e., saturated models of their theory are again beautiful. This yields strict pro-definability of the space of the definable types from any of these classes, in the theory SCVF of separably closed non-trivially valued fields. We also show a separable analog of a classical result of Keisler's, namely that the first order theory of an infinite separable extension $L/K$ of fields -- considered in the pairs language and where the large field $L$ is separably closed, is determined by the theory of the small field $K$ together with the imperfection degree of $L$.

entries.name: Half-delocalization for semiclassical measures of split higher-dimensional quantum cat maps
entries.abstract: We study quantum cat maps on multidimensional tori and prove an optimal lower bound for the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy of their semiclassical measures under the hypothesis that the dynamics splits over the rationals. This is the first instance of such a bound for a dynamical system with multiple positive Lyapunov exponents. The proof is based on a new notion of conditional quantum dynamical entropy and a careful study of the multiple Ehrenfest time adapted to the dynamics.

entries.name: Applying Changes to LDPC Codes by Using 3-Induced Matchings and Eigenvalues
entries.abstract: The 2-switch operation for reducing the number of short cycles in Tanner graphs of LDPC codes has been utilized in some works. If this operation is appropriately applied to a 2-induced matching in a bipartite graph, then it surely preserves the bipartiteness of the graph. With a 2-induced matching, we have only one choice for applying this type of change to the graph. Using 3-induced matchings creates more potential and flexibility to apply certain changes to the Tanner graph. We present a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of a 3-induced matching in bipartite graphs with girth at least 6. A 3-induced matching helps us to have more choices for applying a change to a bipartite graph while surely preserving the bipartiteness of the graph and keeping the degree sequences unchanged. Among all changes that we consider, we select the best change for reducing the number of cycles of length 6. The eigenvalues of subgraphs are used to reach a 3-induced matching, and a condition in some steps can be checked to ensure that the subgraph has at least one 3-induced matching. We present some numerical results regarding the steps at which the condition that guarantees the existence of a 3-induced matching is checked.

entries.name: $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$- and $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$-invariant multidifferential operators
entries.abstract: We determine the dimension of the space of $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$-invariant (n)-ary differential operators on weighted densities for arbitrary weights, including the singular cases in which the usual elimination procedure breaks down. The proof relies on the strong Lefschetz property established by Stanley \cite{s} and Watanabe \cite{w}. We also investigate the corresponding problem in the super case.

entries.name: Quadrature-Induced Local Minima in Structure-Preserving Lotka-Volterra Control
entries.abstract: Harvest quadrature can change a discrete optimal control problem even when the state scheme stays fixed. We study this effect for a positivity-preserving Lotka--Volterra scheme. The difference appears in a model with harvesting alone: rewarding the scheme's removal flux gives a strictly convex reduced cost, whereas using prey density at the start of each step overestimates harvest and can create negative curvature and a strict local minimum that is not global. Rational root isolation certifies the two-step global minimizers. With diffusion in one space dimension, nonnegative bounded $H^1$ initial data and positive diffusivities, the costs, weighted gradients and Hessians differ by $O(τ)$ uniformly in the spatial mesh, where $τ$ is the time step. A uniform positive lower bound on the reduced Hessian gives the same order for the distance between nearby controls. A large enough effort penalty gives unique global discrete minimizers. We also prove positivity, exact population balance and a common variational limit, and derive exact discrete adjoints and Hessian actions. Numerical tests trace changes in curvature and stationary controls across parameters and grids, with costs evaluated on a common reference using adaptive time stepping. The construction extends to weighted production--destruction systems, giving exact harvest accounting and smooth derivatives on fixed grids.

entries.name: Augmented Lagrangian methods with Nesterov acceleration for convex optimization with nonlinear inequality constraints
entries.abstract: In this paper, we develop Nesterov accelerated augmented Lagrangian methods for composite convex optimization with nonlinear inequality constraints. The methods are derived through a compatible discretization of inertial primal-dual dynamics, yielding a unified framework that couples difference extrapolation of the constraint mapping with a projected multiplier. Under convexity and weighted summability of the primal stationarity errors, we prove boundedness of the primal-dual iterates and simultaneous $\mathcal O(k^{-2})$ last-iterate rates for the objective residual and constraint violation. Under strict parameter conditions, the primal-dual sequence converges to a Karush-Kuhn-Tucker pair, and both residuals improve to $o(k^{-2})$. These results require no strong convexity of the objective or constraints. Numerical experiments examine the performance of the proposed methods.

entries.name: A characterisation of almost gentle algebras
entries.abstract: A finite-dimensional algebra over an algebraically closed field is gentle if and only if its trivial extension is special biserial. We prove the corresponding characterisation for almost gentle algebras, that is, an algebra over such a field is almost gentle if and only if its trivial extension is special multiserial, which answers a question of Green and Schroll. As a consequence, the property of having a special multiserial trivial extension is invariant under stable equivalence.

entries.name: An isolated complex Hadamard matrix with nonzero defect
entries.abstract: We exhibit a complex Hadamard matrix of nonzero defect which is isolated among complex Hadamard matrices, up to Hadamard equivalence. This counterexample is realized by a Butson-type Hadamard matrix of size $13$, with entries roots of order $6$ of unity. In the language of commuting squares, this shows that the span condition, previously introduced by the second author as a sufficient condition for isolation, is not a necessary condition for isolation.

entries.name: Planar PArcK is PSPACE-complete
entries.abstract: Partizan Arc Kayles, or PArcK, is a partizan combinatorial game on edge colored graphs, and is a generalization of the game Domineering. Previously, PArcK was shown to be PSPACE-complete on bipartite graphs. In this paper we show that PArcK is PSPACE-complete even when restricted to planar graphs of degree at most three by a reduction from Generalized Hex.

entries.name: Higher-dimensional homogenization of quasiperiodic elastic materials
entries.abstract: Quasiperiodic geometrical arrangements, which exhibit long-range order in the absence of periodicity, have attracted interest in the design of composites and mechanical metamaterials. In this context, direct numerical simulations explicitly resolving the quasiperiodic microstructure become prohibitively expensive for macroscopic problems, motivating the development of homogenized continuum models. However, the absence of a periodic unit cell in physical space hinders the use of conventional homogenization methods. In the present work, we exploit higher-dimensional periodic representations to perform computational homogenization of quasiperiodic elastic composites. Thereby, effective properties are obtained from unit-cell problems solved using the fast Fourier transform in higher-dimensional spaces. Using two-dimensional Penrose tilings and three-dimensional Ammann--Kramer--Neri tilings as paradigmatic examples, we describe the distribution of heterogeneous material properties in the corresponding higher-dimensional unit cells, compute effective elasticity tensors, and assess convergence of fully resolved finite patches to the homogenized limits. We provide open-source implementations of all numerical models.

entries.name: The Estermann Problem with Almost Proportional Summands
entries.abstract: We obtain a family of estimates for short Weyl sums $$ \left| \sum_{x-y<m\le x}e^{2πiαm^n} \right| \ll y\left( \frac{1}{q}+\frac{1}{y}+\frac{q}{y^n} \right)^{\frac{s-1}{s\cdot2^{n-1}}} \bigl(\log(qy)\bigr)^{ \frac{(n-1)^s+s-2}{s\cdot2^{n-1}}}, $$ where $n\ge3$ and $s\ge2$ are fixed integers, $x\ge y\ge2$, $α\in\mathbb R$, $a\in\mathbb Z$, $q\in\mathbb N$, $(a,q)=1$, and $\left|α-\frac{a}{q}\right|\le\frac{1}{q^2}$. For $n\ge4$, we also derive from the modern form of Vinogradov's mean value theorem the estimate $$ \left| \sum_{x-y<m\le x}e^{2πiαm^n} \right| \ll y\left( \frac{1}{q}+\frac{1}{y}+\frac{q}{y^n} \right)^{\frac{1}{n(n-1)+2}} \log y. $$ Using these estimates, repeated Dirichlet approximation, and an estimate in the intermediate range, we establish an asymptotic formula for the number of representations $$ p_1+p_2+m^n=N,\quad |p_i-μ_iN|\le H,\quad i=1,2, \quad |m^n-μ_3N|\le H, $$ where $p_1,p_2$ are primes, $m$ is a positive integer, and $μ_1,μ_2,μ_3$ are fixed positive numbers whose sum is $1$. The asymptotic formula holds in the range $$ N^{1-θ_n}(\log N)^{A_n}\le H\le N^{1-δ}, \qquad θ_n=\min\left\{\frac{1}{2n},\frac{2}{n^2}\right\}, $$ where $0<δ<θ_n$ is fixed, $A_3=3$, $A_4=\frac{61}{4}$, and $A_n=6n-12+\frac{22}{n}-\frac{12}{n^2}$ for $n\ge5$. In the cubic case, the logarithmic exponent in the previously known lower bound for $H$ is reduced from $10$ to $3$. For $n\ge4$, the exponent of $N$ is reduced from $1-\frac{1}{n(n-1)}$ to $1-\frac{2}{n^2}$.

entries.name: Arc connected continua and the double commutant property
entries.abstract: Let $K$ be a compact metrizable space. For $f\in C(K)$ let $M_f$ be the largest lower semicontinuous map with $k\in M_f(k)\subseteq f^{-1}(f(k))$. We say that $K$ has the double commutant property if for every $f\in C(K)$ every continuous function that is constant on all sets $M_f(k)$ is constant on the fibres of $f$; this is exactly the condition that the double commutant of every multiplication operator on $C(K)$ is the closed algebra generated by the operator and the identity. We show that an arc connected continuum has this property if the points having an open locally connected neighbourhood are dense, and we extend this to some continua that are not arc connected. We then develop new techniques that work when such points are not dense, or do not exist at all, and prove that several well-known continua have the property: the Cantor comb, the Cantor fan and, more generally, the cone over every compact metrizable space, every smooth fan with a closed set of end points, and the Cantor grid $(C\times[0,1])\cup([0,1]\times C)$. The property passes to open images. Examples show that the hypotheses cannot be weakened in several directions. For individual functions we show that, on a continuum all of whose arc components are dense, every function that is constant on no arc satisfies the double commutant condition, and that on every smooth dendroid and every fan the functions satisfying it are dense.

entries.name: Causality and order restricted inference in the Aalen additive hasard model
entries.abstract: We study a graphical model (DAG) with time to event as a response variable. We use the Aalen additive hazard model for modelling the effect on the response variable of covariates, combined with a multiple linear regression for earlier layers in a DAG. This enables modelling covariates affecting the event process both directly and indirectly. The indirect component effect is represented by a product $θ_1(t)β_2(t)$, where $θ_1(t)$ describes the effect of the independent covariate on the dependent covariate and $β_2(t)$ is the effect of the dependent covariate on the final time to response variable, in the additive hazard model. We estimate $β_2(t)$ by the order-restricted estimator recently introduced in Anevski and Merai (arXiv:2606.23882v2), thereby enabling disease models with early onset or late onset covariate effects. Combining our previously obtained results with the DAG allows for modelling early onset or late onset covariate effects together with direct and indirect covariate effects, which should be of particular interest for studying causality for complex diseases. We present a nonparametric plug-in estimator of the indirect effect. We derive the limit distribution of the plug-in estimator of the indirect component, and show that it has $n^{1/3}$ pointwise asymptotic rate and a limit distribution which is proportional to the Chernoff distribution.

entries.name: Joint quadratic base changes of elliptic surfaces with torsion Z/4Z and Z/2Z x Z/6Z
entries.abstract: We study elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}(t)$ obtained from an elliptic surface by imposing two quadratic conditions, each of which produces a new point. By the Kani-Rosen decomposition, the joint cover is rational only when the branch loci of the two conditions meet; for two quadratic conditions this means that they share a root. We apply this to two surfaces. For Elkies's rank-four K3 surface with torsion $\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}$, a catalogue of $194$ quadratic conditions contains exactly two such pairs. One recovers the rank-six curve of the authors; the other gives a second, inequivalent curve with torsion $\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}$ and rank six. For the universal curve with torsion $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/6\mathbb{Z}$, $42$ conditions give exactly $21$ rational joint covers, which yield seven curves of rank two. Two more arise from a tower of conditions. Five of these nine curves are the curves of Dujella, Kazalicki and Peral; the other four are not equivalent to any of them. In both cases we determine the Mordell-Weil groups over $\mathbb{Q}(t)$ exactly, and we prove that the curves are pairwise inequivalent under invertible changes of parameter, even over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$.

entries.name: Maximal Independent Sets in Set Systems
entries.abstract: We prove a general theorem on the existence of small maximal independent sets in set systems satisfying natural local density conditions. For an antichain whose degrees are uniform and whose small sets lie in few blocks and whose links overlap little, we show that there is a maximal independent set whose size is asymptotically given by an explicit expression in the degrees, as the degrees grow. The proof comes with a polynomial-time algorithm that finds such a set. This improves on known results for independent sets in uniform hypergraphs; in particular, in a linear uniform hypergraph of large bounded degree, we find an independent set of explicit asymptotic size. Among the applications, we obtain complete arcs in finite projective spaces that come within logarithmic factors of the counting lower bound, improving the known results on Segre's complete arc problem. We also show that, for a wide class of multivariable polynomials, there is a maximal set in a finite field avoiding solutions of the polynomial whose size lies within logarithmic factors of the elementary lower bound.

entries.name: A formally verified convergence theorem for the tug-of-war scheme of the normalized $p$-Laplacian
entries.abstract: We present a complete formalization, using Lean 4, of the convergence of $p$-harmonious functions to the viscosity solution of the Dirichlet problem for the normalized $p$-Laplacian, $2 \le p < \infty$, as the step size goes to zero. By $p$-harmonious functions we mean solutions of the dynamic programming principle of tug-of-war with noise. Our proof follows the argument of Barles and Souganidis and is formalized in full, depending only on Mathlib and the standard axioms of Lean. In particular, we include the asymptotic expansion of the scheme, the viscosity properties of the half-relaxed limits, existence and uniqueness for the discrete problem, the comparison principle and uniqueness for the homogeneous equation, Aleksandrov's theorem, and Jensen's lemma.

entries.name: Higher-Order Isometric Liftings of Convex and Concave Operators
entries.abstract: We study higher-order isometric liftings of bounded operators on Hilbert spaces under convexity and concavity assumptions. First, we prove that every $m$-convex operator $T$ satisfying $\sup_{n\geq 1}n^{-(m-1)}\|T^n\|^2<\infty$ admits a minimal $m$-isometric lifting whose complementary diagonal entry is an expansive $(m-1)$-isometric weighted shift. Next, we show that every $m$-concave operator admits a minimal $m$-isometric lifting with an expansive $m$-isometric weighted-shift component, without imposing an additional growth assumption. We also establish an alternation between convexity and concavity under polynomial growth conditions and give examples illustrating limitations of converse implications.

entries.name: The $k$-th Milnor and Tjurina numbers: conjectures and a bifurcation formula for pairs
entries.abstract: We study the higher-order Milnor and Tjurina numbers of isolated hypersurface singularities and extend these invariants to pairs of plane holomorphic germs. We first show that a conjectured upper bound of Hussain, Yau and Zuo on the ratio between the higher-order Milnor and Tjurina numbers of isolated hypersurface singularities in three-dimensional complex space does not hold: it fails already for the simplest singularity, a non-degenerate quadratic one, and the ratio tends to infinity as the order grows. We then prove that a conjecture of Shi, Yau and Zuo on semiquasihomogeneous singularities holds for plane curves, for every order and over formal power series, and show that it fails in dimension three. Using the theory of higher-order Milnor and Tjurina numbers of foliations in dimension two, we introduce these invariants for pairs of plane germs. For every order, we show that the higher-order Milnor number of a pair is determined by the Milnor number of the pair and the algebraic multiplicity of the associated foliation, and we compute the difference between the higher-order Milnor and Tjurina numbers of the pair. Finally, we establish a bifurcation formula comparing the higher-order Milnor number of a pair with that of the product of the germs. As a consequence, we characterize semitame meromorphic germs as those for which these two numbers agree at some order, or equivalently at every order.

entries.name: Phase Transitions in Heavy-Tailed Mean Estimation under $\ell_p$ Norms
entries.abstract: We study the problem of estimating the mean of a random vector in $\mathbb R^d$ under $\ell_p$ norms, assuming only the existence of a covariance matrix. In the Euclidean norm, the sample mean is already optimal in expectation, and robust estimators are usually needed only to obtain high-probability tails. Our results show that this picture changes for $\ell_p$ norms with $p>2$: robustification is already necessary even for the expected risk. We prove that the minimax risk exhibits a sharp phase transition, controlled by the interaction between the sample size $n$, the dimension $d$, and the norm parameter $p$. In the large-sample regime, the classical Gaussian rate remains achievable. In the complementary regime, heavy-tailed distributions create a genuinely non-Gaussian obstruction. Furthermore we show that the simple estimator: coordinate-wise median of means whose number of buckets chosen according to the geometry of the loss, optimally tracks this phase transition in its expected risk minimax. We also show that natural projection-based median-of-means estimators for general norms, despite achieving the optimal confidence trade-off relative to the sample-mean benchmark of Lugosi and Mendelson (Probab. Theory Relat. Fields, 2019), can be polynomially suboptimal for $\ell_p$ norms even in the constant-probability regime.

entries.name: Discontinuity-Aware Solvers for Vapor-Compression Cycles
entries.abstract: Physics-based models of vapor-compression cycles are often formulated as large, stiff DAE systems with derivative discontinuities introduced at the points of phase change. We use an implementation of a discontinuity-aware ODE and DAE solver scheme that uses domain-specific, user-declared information to compute appropriate time steps for more efficient integration. This scheme is made open-source within DifferentialEquations.jl. We demonstrate how discontinuity information can be specified symbolically in a declarative modeling language such as Dyad and passed to the solver to address the numerical challenges posed. We apply this discontinuity-aware technique to two applications: first, a scalar ODE with two discontinuities, and then a model of a full vapor-compression cycle. The discontinuity-aware solver yields significantly fewer step rejections and improved solver times, particularly with the Rodas5P solver at loose tolerances, as compared to standard error control, suggesting that exposing physical discontinuity information from equation-oriented models to adaptive solvers can improve practical simulation performance without requiring reassembly of the model.

entries.name: Radar Waveform Design via Convex Semidefinite Relaxation
entries.abstract: The ambiguity function (AF) of a radar waveform describes its ability to resolve targets in range and Doppler. Designing a waveform that attains a prescribed AF magnitude is a phase retrieval problem with four trivial ambiguities, and a time- or band-limited pulse is determined up to these ambiguities by at most three times as many AF samples as it has time samples or frequencies. Existing solvers for the narrowband AF, however, are non-convex: they cannot guarantee that they reach the global minimizer, which is unique only up to the trivial ambiguities, so the recovered pulse depends on the starting point. This letter addresses this gap by lifting the problem to positive semidefinite matrices supported on the pulse band, where each AF sample becomes the magnitude of a linear functional. In the lifted space, recovery is formulated as a convex program, and a dual certificate provides a sufficient condition for exactness. The proposed algorithm, wavex, combines an initialization by relaxed reflections, convex semidefinite surrogate steps, and a local polish. Numerical experiments show that wavex accurately recovers band-limited pulses from complete AFs and from AFs with most of their samples removed, provided the remaining samples determine the pulse, and that its accuracy degrades gracefully as the noise increases. wavex is built on the open-source library invexapi, and the code that reproduces every result is available at https://github.com/samuelpinilla/waveX.

entries.name: Unirationality of Meromorphic Differential Strata
entries.abstract: We prove that all components of the meromorphic differential strata are unirational in genus $2\le g\le 5$ and with relatively low number of poles. In particular, it follows that the moduli space of pointed even spin curves $\mathcal{S}_{5;1}^+=\mathcal{S}_5^+\times_{\mathcal{M}_5}\mathcal{M}_{5,1}$ is unirational.

entries.name: Two categorifications of the Kekulé relations
entries.abstract: We give new relations in the kernel of the foam evaluation. As a consequence we obtain categorifications of all the Kelulé relations introduced by Morrison. Along the way, we discover an equivalent set of relations for which we provide categorifications as well.

entries.name: Curves in $\PP^{3}$ are Complete Intersections or Golod
entries.abstract: Let $I\subset S$ be an unmixed, codimension 2 ideal in a regular local ring, or an unmixed, codimension 2 ideal that is homogeneous in a positively graded polynomial ring over a field. We prove the statement of the title when $\pd_{S}(S/I) \leq 3$, and conjecture that this dichotomy holds in codimension 2 with any projective dimension.

entries.name: The Maxwell Bethe-Sommerfeld problem I: Thin-layer induction and results for planar TE modes
entries.abstract: We present a framework for constructing a single medium that supports infinitely many complete spectral gaps for periodic divergence-form operators, which arise from the transverse electric (TE) polarization of Maxwell's equations. The construction proceeds by inductively inserting a seed medium with a prescribed spectral gap into a thin layer of the unit cell. As a result, we obtain densely many counterexamples to the Bethe-Sommerfeld Conjecture (BSC) for divergence-form operators. Moreover, we prove that the thin-layer construction controls the gap topology: by carefully selecting the seed medium, one can realize a single operator with any prescribed configuration of gap Chern numbers. This is the first of two papers that contains all the fundamental ingredients for the thin-layer induction. In the second paper, we will apply this framework to disprove the BSC for the full three-dimensional Maxwell operator.

entries.name: Integral zero-sum incidence identities and Davenport constants in rank three
entries.abstract: We study the Davenport constant of finite abelian groups through signed identities among zero-sum subsequences. An integral incidence identity of degree $t$ for a sequence assigns integer weights to its nonempty zero-sum subsequences so that the weights add up to one, while those of the subsequences containing any given nonempty set of at most $t$ terms add up to zero. Over a finite abelian $p$-group $H$, the zero-sum subsequences of a sequence of any length have an indicator polynomial of degree at most $D(H)-1$, and this gives a transfer principle: if, for each $t\ge0$, every sequence of $L(t)$ terms over $Q$ admits such an identity of degree $t$, then $D(Q\oplus H)\le L(D(H)-1)$ for every finite abelian $p$-group $H$. For $m\in\{2,3,4\}$ we construct integral identities at length $L(t)=m(t+3)-2$ over $C_m^3$, and prove that these thresholds are sharp over fields of characteristic zero or characteristic not dividing $m$. For a prime $p\nmid m$ and $0\le a\le b\le c$, we prove that \[ D(C_{mp^a}\oplus C_{mp^b}\oplus C_{mp^c}) =m(p^a+p^b+p^c)-2. \] In particular $D(C_{15}^3)=43$ and $D(C_{20}^3)=58$, which are the two smallest cases of the conjecture $D(C_n^3)=3n-2$ left open in the literature. The proofs of the base cases for $m \in \{3,4\}$ are computer-assisted. All of the results in this paper have been formalised in Lean 4.

entries.name: Learning Advantage Function Surrogates via Convex Conjugate Matching
entries.abstract: A policy trained to make per-unit decisions, such as how much of a product to order, tells us the best action but not the cost of deviating from it. That cost, the advantage function, is what downstream systems need when they have to depart from the per-unit optimum: to estimate the impact of ordering more or fewer units, to respond to a one-off vendor discount, or to satisfy a shared capacity constraint. The advantage function is what makes such trade-offs computable, yet pure policy-learning algorithms often produce the policy alone, without a critic that would yield it. We propose a method to train an advantage function surrogate through price perturbations motivated by a Fenchel-Young loss. We describe a two-stage recipe (fit the policy, then the cost model) and illustrate it on a multi-period inventory management problem.

entries.name: A feedback-driven central limit theorem with $q$-Gaussian limits
entries.abstract: We establish a central limit theorem, the feedback-driven central limit theorem, for sums whose summands are independent noise variables multiplied by an amplitude that depends on the preceding normalized sum $y$. The summands are martingale differences whose conditional variance, $c+b\,y^{2}$, depends quadratically on $y$, with feedback strength $b$; unlike in the martingale central limit theorem, this conditional variance does not settle to a constant. The noise has finite variance; for positive feedback we assume, as in Lyapunov's theorem, a finite third moment, and for negative feedback bounded noise, so that the conditional variance stays nonnegative. For positive feedback, the normalized sum converges to a Student law, equivalently a $q$-Gaussian with $1<q<2$, independently of the noise distribution. For negative feedback, it converges to a compactly supported density, which is a $q$-Gaussian with $q<1$ when $-\tfrac12<b<0$. The Gaussian law, $q=1$, is recovered at zero feedback, while the Cauchy law, $q=2$, is obtained only as a limiting case, in a triangular array in which the feedback grows slowly with the number of terms. Thus every $q<2$ is obtained for a fixed feedback strength, and $q=2$ as a limit. We further show that the balance identity behind the theorem singles out quadratic feedback: a $q$-Gaussian with $q<2$ satisfies it only for a quadratic conditional variance, and no $q$-Gaussian with $2\le q<3$ satisfies it for any conditional variance. The proofs use the method of moments for negative feedback and a Wasserstein coupling argument for positive feedback, including cases in which the limiting variance is infinite.

entries.name: Independent set reconfiguration is hard at treewidth four
entries.abstract: Independent Set Reconfiguration asks whether one of two given independent sets of equal size can be transformed into the other by moving one token at a time while keeping the occupied vertices independent. In token sliding, a token moves along an edge. In token jumping, it may move to any unoccupied vertex. For both rules, the problem is solvable in polynomial time on trees and is PSPACE-complete on graphs of treewidth at most $c$ for some fixed constant $c$. For each rule, the smallest treewidth bound that suffices for hardness has long been open. We narrow this gap by proving that both versions are NP-hard on graphs of treewidth four.

entries.name: Long time derivation of the Boltzmann equation from dynamics of short-range potentials
entries.abstract: We derive the Boltzmann equation from the Newtonian dynamics of particles interacting through a short-range repulsive potential for arbitrarily long times, in the Boltzmann--Grad limit. This extends the recent hard-sphere result of Deng, Hani and Ma (arXiv:2408.07818) to short-range potentials. Compared with hard spheres, two new difficulties arise: (i) in the absence of a Burago--Ferleger--Kononenko-type bound (Ann. of Math. 147 (1998), 695--708, doi:10.2307/120962), a bounded number of particles may undergo an unbounded number of collisions within a short time; and (ii) since collisions last a positive time, three or more particles may interact simultaneously. To overcome (i), we treat such clusters of recollisions as single objects, called boxes, keeping track only of their entry and exit structure, so that internal collisions do not enter the combinatorial counting. The multi-particle collisions in (ii), together with the boxes, lead to more complicated molecules, which requires adapting the counting estimates and the cutting algorithm.

entries.name: Counterfactual Screening of Rare Secondary Overloads in Power Grids with a Stochastic Surrogate for Electromagnetic Transient Simulations
entries.abstract: Power-system operators continually ask what would happen if a component failed now. Single-phase-to-ground faults cleared by single-pole tripping and automatic reclosure usually have no lasting consequences. In rare cases, however, the transient excited during the open-phase interval drives distant lines or transformers into overload that persists after the faulted line is restored. We develop a counterfactual screening framework for these secondary overloads, combining a linear stochastic swing surrogate with cross-entropy importance sampling. The surrogate represents the open-phase corridor through an effective coupling factor and localized multiplicative noise, with both parameters learned from electromagnetic-transient (EMT) simulations rather than prescribed. Closed-form propagation of the mean and covariance permits deterministic calibration without Monte Carlo sampling. On the reduced WECC 240-bus system, a globally calibrated model substantially improves finite-time agreement with the EMT electromechanical state. The global models are calibrated at reclosure and tested on disjoint faulted lines under a longer open-phase interval. Line- and operating-state-specific models use additional reclosure data from the assessment lines and provide smaller further gains at the cost of more separate fits. The fitted coupling is lower than the phase-counting baseline, consistent with the direction anticipated by sequence-network analysis. Cross-entropy importance sampling directs computational effort toward contingencies associated with persistent overload and yields rare-event probability estimates together with a map linking initiating faults to the elements they endanger. By separating offline EMT calibration from repeated surrogate evaluation, the method supports probabilistic contingency screening and identifies where detailed high-fidelity assessment is most valuable.

entries.name: Decorated lattices: hyperuniformity and limit theorems
entries.abstract: We introduce \emph{decorated lattices}, a point process obtained by placing finite random point configurations in lattice cells. A stationary mark field selects the motif laws and acts as a random environment transmitting dependence between cells, while allowing flexible local arrangements. Using this construction, one can efficiently generate large regions of disordered patterns with desired local behavior while the random environment controls the asymptotic density fluctuations. Under moment and summability assumptions, we derive an explicit decomposition of the Bartlett spectral measure into contributions from conditional motif fluctuations and correlations between marks. This yields criteria for hyperuniformity, or generally $p$-uniformity. Independent, nondegenerate count fluctuations destroy hyperuniformity, whereas suitable dependence governed by the random environment can restore it despite random and unequal cell counts. Once count fluctuations are sufficiently suppressed, motif geometry and its spatial correlations govern the finer order of uniformity. Under mixing assumptions, we also establish central limit theorems for linear statistics, with fluctuations governed by cell counts or, at a finer scale, by the first spatial moments of the motifs.

entries.name: Hausdorff continuity of logarithmic and Riesz capacities
entries.abstract: Let $E_n$ be $α_n$-uniformly perfect compact sets that converge to a compact set $E$ in the Hausdorff distance $d_n=d_H(E_n,E)$. We prove that the logarithmic capacity of $E_n$ converges to that of $E$ whenever $\log(1/α_n)=O(\log(1/d_n))$ and that no factor tending to infinity can be inserted in this bound. A common energy-transfer theorem also yields Hausdorff continuity of Riesz capacity under local capacity bounds, including bounds obtained from lower Hausdorff content density. Finally, we correct our earlier claims about the uniform convergence of Green functions.

entries.name: Feasibility certificates for DeePC: A set invariance approach
entries.abstract: DeePC is posed on a window of past inputs and outputs, so its feasible set is a set of histories and is not available in closed form. We write the DeePC solution as an implicit ReLU network whose weights are built from Hankel matrices and whose activation patterns are the critical regions of the underlying quadratic program. This gives, directly from the Hankel matrices, the feasible set of DeePC as a polyhedral projection, its explicit piecewise-affine control law, and an exact linear model of the history window. We compute three invariant sets of histories: the maximal positively invariant set of the unsaturated linear branch, the region of recursive feasibility of DeePC without terminal ingredients, and the maximal control invariant set of admissible histories. We show these sets are nested and provide numerical examples.

entries.name: Lengths and Counting of Palindromic Prefixes of Standard Sturmian Words
entries.abstract: Every standard Sturmian word $c_\mathbf{d}$ is determined by a directive sequence $\mathbf{d}=(d_i)_{i\ge 1}$ of positive integers, and its palindromic prefixes are obtained by iterated palindromic closure. We describe the lengths of these prefixes by the numbers $j\,\ell_{i-1}+\ell_{i-2}-2$, where $\ell_n$ is the length of the $n$-th standard word and $1\le j\le d_i$, and we show that each nonzero length is attained by exactly one pair $(i,j)\neq(1,1)$. For a purely periodic directive sequence of period $k$ we then prove that the number $π_\mathbf{d}(N)$ of nonempty palindromic prefixes of length at most $N$ satisfies \[ π_\mathbf{d}(N)\sim\frac{d_1+\cdots+d_k}{\logλ_\mathbf{d}}\,\log N, \] where $λ_\mathbf{d}$ is the largest eigenvalue of the matrix $M(d_1)\cdots M(d_k)$. For the Fibonacci word this gives $π_\mathbf{d}(N)\sim\log N/\log\varphi$, where $\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$.

entries.name: Averaging for multi-scale McKean-Vlasov equation
entries.abstract: We consider a system of Stochastic Differential Equations with two time scales, so called slow-fast system of SDEs. As customary when studying slow-fast dynamics, we seek a coarse grained description of the system, obtained, in the limit of scale separation, by 'averaging out' the fast component of the dynamics (so-called averaging limit). We study slow-fast systems where the fast variable is described by a process which is non-linear in the sense of McKean i.e. by an SDE whose coefficients depend on the law of the process itself, while the slow variable is a linear SDE (linear in the sense of McKean). We show that, when the fast variable is a McKean-Vlasov process and, additionally, the coefficients of the SDE depend on the position of the slow process, the limit of scale separation is not provided by the usual ansatz which one would expect by applying classical averaging paradigms. We identify the limit and provide complete proof.

entries.name: The classification of $2$-dimensional rigid algebras
entries.abstract: Using the algebraic classification of all $2$-dimensional algebras, we give the algebraic classification of all $2$-dimensional rigid, conservative and terminal algebras over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0. We have the geometric classification of the variety of $2$-dimensional terminal algebras, and based on the geometric classification of these algebras we formulate some open problems.

entries.name: The Riemann hypothesis
entries.abstract: The Weyl symbolic calculus of operators leads to the construction, if one takes for symbol a certain distribution decomposing over the zeros of the Riemann zeta function, of an operator with the following property: the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the validity of a collection of estimates involving this operator. Pseudodifferential arithmetic, a novel chapter of pseudodifferential operator theory, makes it possible to make the operator under study fully explicit. This leads to a proof of the conjecture.

entries.name: A Chebotarev Density Theorem over Local Fields
entries.abstract: We compute the $p$-adic densities of points with a given splitting type along a (generically) finite map, analogous to the classical Chebotarev theorem over number fields and function fields. Under some mild hypotheses, we prove that these densities satisfy a functional equation in the size of the residue field. This functional equation is a direct reflection of Poincaré duality in étale cohomology. As a consequence, we prove a conjecture of Bhargava, Cremona, Fisher, and Gajović on factorization densities of p-adic polynomials. The key tool is the notion of admissible pairs associated to a group, which we use as an invariant of the inertia and decomposition action of a local field on the fibers of the finite map. We compute the splitting densities by Möbius inverting certain p-adic integrals along the poset of admissible pairs. The conjecture on factorization densities follows immediately for tamely ramified primes from our general results. We reduce the complete conjecture to the existence of an explicit "Tate-type" resolution of the "resultant locus" over the integers and complete the proof of the conjecture by constructing this resolution.

entries.name: On minimal subshifts of linear word complexity with slope less than 3/2
entries.abstract: We prove that every infinite minimal subshift with word complexity $p(q)$ satisfying $\limsup p(q)/q < 3/2$ is measure-theoretically isomorphic to its maximal equicontinuous factor; in particular, it has measurably discrete spectrum. Among other applications, this provides a proof of Sarnak's conjecture for all subshifts with $\limsup p(q)/q < 3/2$ (which can be thought of as a much stronger version of zero entropy). We also show that all such subshifts are balanced, and that orbit equivalence between them is characterized by the additive eigenvalue group. As in [CP23], our main technique is proving that all low-complexity minimal subshifts have a specific type of representation via a sequence $\{τ_k\}$ of substitutions, usually called an S-adic decomposition. The maximal equicontinuous factor is the (possibly twisted) product of an odometer with a rotation on a compact abelian connected one-dimensional group (either a circle or solenoid), for which we can give an explicit description in terms of the substitutions $τ_k$. We also prove that all such odometers and groups may appear for minimal subshifts with $\limsup p(q)/q = 1$, demonstrating that lower complexity thresholds do not further restrict the possible structure.

entries.name: A generalized Schmidt's subspace theorem for algebraic points of bounded degree
entries.abstract: Schmidt's subspace theorem in terms of Seshadri constants for closed subschemes in subgeneral position has already been richly developed. Building upon this framework, we establish a Schmidt subspace theorem for algebraic points of bounded degree with respect to numerically equivalent ample divisors, attaining the optimal factor known to date and deriving a generalized weighted version. Also, we settle a long-standing conjecture in this field.

entries.name: Non-algebraicity of non-abundant foliations and abundance for adjoint foliated structures
entries.abstract: Assuming the abundance conjecture in dimension $d$, we establish a non-algebraicity criterion of foliations: any log canonical foliation of rank $\le d$ with $ν\neqκ$ is not algebraically integrable, answering question of Ambro--Cascini--Shokurov--Spicer. Under the same hypothesis, we prove abundance for klt algebraically integrable adjoint foliated structures of dimension $\le d$ and show the existence of good minimal models or Mori fiber spaces. In particular, when $d=3$, all these results hold unconditionally. Using similar arguments, we solve a problem proposed by Lu and Wu on abundance of surface adjoint foliated structures that are not necessarily algebraically integrable.

entries.name: Non-Stationary Difference Equation and Affine Laumon Space III: Generalization to $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$
entries.abstract: In a series of papers, we have considered a non-stationary difference equation which was originally discovered for the deformed Virasoro conformal block. The equation involves mass parameters and, when they are tuned appropriately, the equation is regarded as a quantum KZ equation for $U_q\bigl(A_{1}^{(1)}\bigr)$. We introduce a $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ generalization of the non-stationary difference equation. The Hamiltonian is expressed in terms of $q$-commuting variables and allows both factorized forms and a normal ordered form. By specializing the mass parameters appropriately, the Hamiltonian can be identified with the $R$-matrix of the symmetric tensor representation of $U_q\bigl(A_{N-1}^{(1)}\bigr)$, which in turn comes from the 3D (tetrahedron) $R$-matrix. We conjecture that the affine Laumon partition function of type $A_{N-1}^{(1)}$ gives a solution to our $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ non-stationary difference equation. As a check of our conjecture, we work out the four-dimensional limit and find that the non-stationary difference equation reduces to the Fuji-Suzuki-Tsuda system.

entries.name: Campana separable rational connectedness of toric orbifold
entries.abstract: Campana introduced a notion of Campana rational connectedness for Campana orbifolds and conjectured that certain Fano orbifolds are Campana rationally connected. In this paper, we study a version of this conjecture in positive characteristic and verify a stronger statement for some toric orbifolds. We also provide examples illustrating the relation between the failure of separable Campana rational connectedness and singularities.

entries.name: On the effective Yau--Tian--Donaldson conjecture for projective bundles
entries.abstract: Consider the projectivization $\mathbb{P}(E)$ of a holomorphic vector bundle $E$ over a smooth curve, equipped with a fixed Kähler class $[ω]$. Our first main result establishes that the existence of an extremal Kähler metric in $[ω]$ is equivalent to the weighted stability of a moment polytope $Δ$ with respect to explicit weight functions depending on the topological data of $\mathbb{P}(E)$. We then introduce a class of test configurations, which we call compatible test configurations. These are constructed by gluing horospherical test configurations of the fibers, arising from convex functions on $Δ$ via Delcroix's construction, to the principal bundle associated with $\mathbb{P}(E)$. Our second main result shows that the weighted stability of $Δ$ naturally arises when computing the relative uniform K-stability of $[ω]$ with respect to compatible test configurations.

entries.name: Every 3-connected $\{K_{1,4},K_{1,4}+e\}$-free split graph of order at least 13 is Hamilton-connected
entries.abstract: A graph is split if its vertex set can be partitioned into a clique and an independent set. Let $K_{1,4}+e$ denote the graph obtained from $K_{1,4}$ by adding an edge between two leaves. Ryjáček et al. [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 134 (2019), 239--263] conjectured that every $4$-connected graph with minimum degree at least 6 that contains neither $K_{1,4}$ nor $K_{1,4}+e$ as an induced subgraph is Hamiltonian. They proved the conclusion for $5$-connected graphs with the same minimum degree bound. We prove that every $3$-connected split graph of order at least 13 that contains neither of these induced subgraphs is Hamilton-connected. Together with Dirac's theorem, this proves the conjecture of Ryjáček et al. for split graphs.

entries.name: The Ferrers bound for spanning trees in bipartite graphs
entries.abstract: We prove Ehrenborg's conjecture that every connected bipartite graph $G$ with parts of size $m$ and $n$ has at most $\frac{1}{mn}\prod_{v\in V(G)} \operatorname{deg}(v)$ spanning trees, and that equality holds if and only if $G$ is a Ferrers graph.

entries.name: A Non-graded Koszul Duality and Its Applications
entries.abstract: Let \(Λ\) be a finite-dimensional Koszul algebra with Koszul dual \(Λ^!\). We establish derived Koszul dualities at the level of bounded derived categories, both in the graded setting \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(Λ\textup{-gmod})\) and in the ungraded setting \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(Λ\textup{-mod})\). We first prove a graded derived Koszul duality for every finite-dimensional Koszul algebra, with no Noetherian or coherence assumptions on the Koszul dual. We then show that the bounded derived category \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(Λ\textup{-mod})\) can be reconstructed from the graded theory as the triangulated hull of an orbit category. This yields a genuinely non-graded derived Koszul duality. We further establish singular and dg refinements of these dualities. For Iwanaga--Gorenstein Koszul algebras, this gives a stable Koszul duality for graded Gorenstein-projective modules and their ungraded counterparts, providing a non-graded form of the Bernstein--Gel'fand--Gel'fand correspondence. As applications, we obtain new descriptions of the bounded derived categories \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(\mathcal{O}_λ)\) for all integral blocks of category \(\mathcal{O}\), including singular blocks, which are non-graded counterparts of the Koszul dualities of Beilinson, Ginzburg, and Soergel. We also establish analogous dualities for certain categories of perverse sheaves arising in geometric representation theory. Finally, we formulate conjectural descriptions of bounded derived and singularity categories of finite-dimensional graded algebras in terms of dg orbit categories.

entries.name: On small-step quarter plane lattice walks with a non D-finite univariate generating function
entries.abstract: We report on the status of the conjecture of Bousquet-Mélou and Mishna that the univariate counting generating function of a small-step quarter-plane lattice model is D-finite if and only if a particular group associated to the walk is finite. While the finite-group case is fully resolved, the infinite-group case remains incomplete. First we survey the known cases. By invoking asymptotics results from probability theory and a case analysis completed by Bostan, Raschel and Salvy (2014), we establish that the generating functions of 14 infinite-group models are not D-finite, and that for an additional 18 models the generating function for walks that end on an axis is not D-finite. We conclude with a discussion of limitations of asymptotic arguments to resolve the remaining cases.

entries.name: One Shot, Twenty-One Balls: A Computer-Assisted Proof of a Single-Stroke Total Clearance in an Idealized Model of Snooker
entries.abstract: Snooker folklore holds that no single stroke can pocket all twenty-one object balls. We examine the claim in an explicit model: twenty-two equal disks on a rectangle with six pocket points, under constant rolling deceleration, frictionless collisions with normal restitution, and lossy specular cushions. We exhibit a configuration and a stroke, and prove in interval arithmetic that every stroke in an explicit box around it pockets all twenty-one object balls, so the set of successful strokes has positive measure. That set is a ribbon: every speed from 9.3214 to 12 m/s works, while the certified window of directions is 9.481e-43 radians wide, a number explained by a first-order analysis of twenty near-grazing collisions. A second configuration, a near-frozen cluster, has a certified window 9.4e-4 radians wide, thirty-nine orders of magnitude wider; its certificate uses Taylor models of degree six. The strokes with a given list of events form a semialgebraic set, and the endpoints of the windows are algebraic points of the circle. For the regulation opening position we state the corresponding conjecture, and show that if it holds with a regular witness then a finite certified search establishes it.

entries.name: The Bias Conjecture for One-Parameter, Non-Isotrivial Elliptic Curve Families
entries.abstract: We investigate Miller's bias conjecture for general one-parameter families of elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ with non-constant $j$-invariants. Utilizing methods developed by Michel, we view the second moment as the sum of distinct cohomological components: a main $p^2$ term, a $p^{3/2}$ term arising from the first cohomology over the projective line, and terms of order $p$ or lower corresponding to singular fibers. By assuming the generalized Sato-Tate conjecture, we employ representation and motive theory to demonstrate that the coefficient of the $p^{3/2}$ term averages to zero in the limit. We then independently analyze the lower-order contributions without assuming Sato-Tate. By applying the Chebotarev density theorem and analyzing Galois representations, we show that the contributions to the order $p$ term from additive singular fibers average to a non-positive value. Consequently, the only remaining average contribution to the $p$ term is $-B_pp$, where $B_p$ denotes the number of ``bad'' points where the discriminant vanishes. Because $B_p$ averages to a strictly positive value, the overall coefficient of the $p$ term averages to a strictly negative value in the limit, thereby establishing the bias conjecture for these families.

entries.name: Strong transport noise prevents self-intersection in 2D fluid-structure interaction
entries.abstract: We consider the interaction of a viscous incompressible fluid with a flexible elastic shell occupying the boundary of the fluid's domain in two space dimensions. The shell is modelled by a visco-elastic linearised beam equation. It is an open problem in fluid-structure interaction, if a self-intersection of the structure can be excluded in the long run. We show that by adding a physically well-motived and sufficiently strong transport noise in the structure equation, the self-intersection does not occur before any given end-time with any prescribed probability smaller than 1.

entries.name: Hook monomial immanants are Kazhdan-Lusztig positive
entries.abstract: Stembridge conjectured that every monomial immanant is non-negative on totally non-negative matrices, and Haiman proposed a stronger statement which at $q=1$ says that every monomial immanant is a non-negative integer combination of the Kazhdan-Lusztig immanants of Rhoades and Skandera. We prove this for every hook shape $(a,1^{n-a})$ and every $n$.
